messages:
anna_infra: quick q — i'm wiring the PrivateLink for analytics-saas. we need inbound DNS forwarding so customer VPCs can resolve our internal svc names (svc.internal.redwood). proposing pattern: create a private hosted zone in infra account, then use Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints + resolver rules in infra, and inbound endpoints in customer account that forward back to infra. is that the recommended approach? cc @samir @tanya

samir: short answer: yes, that's the common pattern. couple notes: resolver endpoints are per-AZ (ENIs) and costy, and resolver rules live in the account where the rule is created. pattern we use elsewhere:
```
# infra account
resource "aws_route53_resolver_endpoint" "outbound" { direction = "OUTBOUND" vpc_id = aws_vpc.infra.id ip_address { subnet_id = aws_subnet.infra_az1.id } ip_address { subnet_id = aws_subnet.infra_az2.id } }
resource "aws_route53_resolver_rule" "to_customer" { domain_name = "customer.internal." rule_type = "FORWARD" resolver_endpoint_id = aws_route53_resolver_endpoint.outbound.id target_ip { ip = "10.0.50.10" } }
# in customer account you create an inbound endpoint and share the IPs with infra for the rule target
```
this avoids sharing private hosted zones cross-account. instead we forward the zone to the customer's inbound endpoints.

tanya: small clarification — are we creating a private hosted zone in infra for svc.internal.redwood AND also creating rules in infra that forward the zone to customer inbound endpoints? or do we create the private zone in the customer and associate with infra VPCs?

samir: we keep the authoritative private hosted zone in infra (our svc records). customers should not host the same zone. infra's resolver handles queries we receive from customer VPCs by forwarding them to our engines or returning answers. the flow for customer->infra typically is: customer VPC DNS -> customer resolver outbound (if they have) -> customer inbound endpoint -> VPC endpoint private link -> infra. but with PrivateLink you often stitch using resolver rules rather than direct PrivateLink for DNS. for privatelink endpoints (interface ENIs) we also have to ensure the endpoint's security group allows inbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) from customer resolver ENIs.

lee: iirc for k8s: apps inside customer k8s need kube-dns/CoreDNS to forward the specific zone to the VPC resolver IP (the inbound endpoint IP). we do this by updating the coredns ConfigMap, e.g.:
```
redwood.internal:53 {
  forward . 10.0.5.10
}
```
otherwise pods will use cluster DNS and never reach the resolver.

anna_infra: thanks — what about Terraform organization? do we add the resolver resources to the privatelink module, or make a separate resolver module per-account? also secrets for the zone delegation / validation?

samir: prefer separate module: route53-resolver module which takes target IPs (customer inbound) as inputs. keep privatelink/endpoint-service separate. flow: customer account creates inbound endpoint via their infra TF (we have a minimal customer onboarding module), outputs inbound endpoint IPs in a secure SSM parameter or a secret that infra can read (or ownership-approved cross-account data share). then infra's route53-resolver module consumes those IPs to create forward rules. avoid storing plaintext IPs in the monorepo — use secure param store.

anna_infra: practical question — can we automagically register the privatelink interface ENI IPs in the resolver rule target? or do we need to use the customer-provided inbound endpoint IPs?

samir: you need inbound endpoints in the customer account. Interface endpoints (Privatelink) are not DNS resolvers — they are L4/L7 endpoints. resolver rules must point to resolver inbound endpoints' IPs (the ones that answer DNS). that means onboarding requires the customer to create the inbound endpoint and either add the IPs to a shared SSM or grant us a cross-account role to read them.

aws-deploy-bot: created aws_route53_resolver_endpoint.outbound (rsl-out-abc123) in infra-vpc-1 — pending ENI attachments in az-a, az-b

tanya: also remember to add security group rules: allow TCP/UDP 53 from customer inbound ENI ranges and from our k8s nodes if they will forward directly. and update the endpoint-service policy to allow the customer's aws account if using interface endpoints.

anna_infra: got it. i'll draft a PR with two terraform modules: customers/onboard -> creates inbound endpoint and outputs IPs (stored in SSM param with kms), and infra/route53-resolver -> creates outbound+rules reading those SSM params. will link PR in a bit for review. :thumbsup:

samir: sg, ping me once PR is up and i'll do a quick tf review for edge cases (timeouts, deletion order for resolver rules).

anna_infra: PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/789 — includes sample terraform and a k8s coredns snippet in docs. tagging @samir @lee for review.

lee: quick lgtm on the coredns snippet, i'll test in staging tomorrow and report back.
